stem: A hedge fund reports five annual returns (%): 5, −3, 8, 1 and 4. The unbiased sample variance of these returns (in %²) is closest to:
explanation: Mean = 3. Squared deviations: 4, 36, 25, 4, 1, summing to 70. s² = 70/(5 − 1) = 17.5.

rationale.A: Incorrect. 14.0 divides by n = 5, giving the biased estimator.
rationale.B: Incorrect. 4.18 is the sample standard deviation √17.5, not the variance.
rationale.C: Correct. Dividing the sum of squared deviations by n − 1 = 4 gives 17.5.
rationale.D: Incorrect. 3.74 is √14, the square root of the biased variance.

stem: A strategy's monthly returns have a sample standard deviation of 1.2%. Based on 36 monthly observations, the standard error of the sample mean return is closest to:

rationale.A: Incorrect. 0.03% divides by n = 36 instead of √36 = 6.
rationale.B: Correct. Divide the standard deviation by the square root of the sample size: 1.2/6 = 0.20%.
rationale.C: Incorrect. 1.20% is the standard deviation of individual returns, not of the sample mean.
rationale.D: Incorrect. 7.20% multiplies by √n instead of dividing.

stem: An analyst estimates return variance by dividing the sum of squared deviations from the sample mean by n rather than n − 1. Which description of this estimator is most accurate?
explanation: Its expectation is (n − 1)σ²/n, below σ², so it is biased downward. The bias factor tends to 1 as n grows, so it is consistent.

rationale.A: Incorrect. Its expected value is (n − 1)σ²/n, not σ², so it is biased.
rationale.B: Incorrect. The bias is downward, because deviations from the fitted mean understate dispersion, and the estimator converges to σ².
rationale.C: Incorrect. It is biased in finite samples, and it is consistent rather than inconsistent.
rationale.D: Correct. Biased low in finite samples, but the bias vanishes as n increases, so it is consistent.

stem: Daily returns on a credit portfolio are iid, strongly right-skewed and have a finite variance. A risk analyst computes the mean of 500 daily returns. According to the central limit theorem:
options: the distribution of the sample mean is approximately normal, even though individual returns are skewed.
the individual daily returns become approximately normally distributed as the sample grows.
the sample mean has the same skewness as the individual returns regardless of sample size.
the sample mean converges to zero because positive and negative returns cancel out.
explanation: The CLT concerns the sampling distribution of the mean: with iid data and finite variance, the standardised sample mean is approximately standard normal for large n.

rationale.A: Correct. The CLT applies to the sample mean, not the underlying data.
rationale.B: Incorrect. The data keep their own skewed distribution; collecting more of them does not change it.
rationale.C: Incorrect. Skewness of the sample mean shrinks as n grows, which is why it approaches the normal.
rationale.D: Incorrect. The law of large numbers says the sample mean converges to the true mean μ, not to zero.
